judgements.justification: A's meta-review leans on the area chair's own reading ('pushes forward the research') and gives no reason for a spotlight, though no A reviewer rated above 7 or argued for a higher tier.
A's area chair praised the paper's advance in its own area but forecast no impact beyond the paper's setting.
The rebuttal lifted A's Reviewer_vTqw to 7 ('My concerns are well addressed'), while no B reviewer replied or visibly moved and c6Mx's 4 stood.
Two of A's three supporting reviews were thin: KmGd (2 h, confidence 2, three lines) and Dzyq (no specific point); B's critics c6Mx and TpjV were confidence 4 with specific claims.

Only B raised the incrementality of the l2 GLL result (1-D smoothing plus [FKT20], conceded by the authors) and the novelty of the private Frank-Wolfe; these held B at poster, and no A reviewer raised them.
Both committees flagged the fragmented, hard-to-read set of results and saw the weaker l2 rate than [ZCH+20]; A's area chair ignored both, while B's made fragmentation its main message.
B's meta-review mentions discussion, but the record shows no score change attributed to other reviewers' views in either committee.
No reviewer's rating clearly contradicts the verdict of their own text.
A's low-confidence KmGd gave 6 and B's Brcd gave 7, but neither committee's mean was held near the threshold by unsure reviewers in a way that separates the tiers; A went higher.
B's area chair echoed a concern shared by c6Mx, MuL7 and Brcd, not one outlier, and A's cited no reviewer.
Without the detractor B's reviewers scored at least as high as A's (mean 7.0 against 6.67); there is no calibration gap on similar verdicts.
A's 7, 6, 7, with no detractor and no reviewer above 7 or arguing for a spotlight, became a spotlight, while B's spread (4 to 8, with the only 8) held it at poster.
vTqw rose on a refined bound that the camera-ready Theorem 11 carries and on standard proof answers, not on unchecked copied results.
A's meta-review names no weakness, although KmGd and Dzyq flagged readability and too many results; B's meta-review carried the fragmentation concern forward.
c6Mx's wrong weakly convex argument is a side point; the 4 rests mainly on the two claims the paper confirms, and vTqw's wrong l_p claim was withdrawn without effect.
The authors told A's vTqw that [ZCH+20] has better sample complexity, yet vTqw raised to 7 and A's area chair gave a spotlight without mentioning it.
No objection or score cut came after the response period in either committee.
The score profiles differ (7, 6, 7 against 7, 4, 8, 6), and A's area chair relied on own reading, not a cut-off on near-identical scores.
Neither area chair set aside a best-informed reviewer: A's vTqw ended at 7 in line with the outcome, and B's poster matches its confidence-4 reviewers' 4 and 6.
A's only technical concerns were clarifications the authors answered, lifting vTqw; B's main concerns were incrementality and novelty, which the authors could only concede.
B's detractor Reviewer_c6Mx (4) alone pulled B's mean from 7.0 to 6.25; B's other reviewers (7, 8, 6) matched or exceeded A's 7, 6, 7.
c6Mx did not reply, but the response conceded its two main points rather than answering them, so the 4's basis was not answered.

reasoning: Stage 1 finds A's spotlight the anomaly: a 7, 6, 7 panel with two thin reviews and no detractor, a meta-review that gives no reason for the tier and drops the readability weaknesses, and a rebuttal that answered A's only technical reviewer. B drew confident critics whose incrementality case the paper confirms, and its single detractor alone moved its mean below A's. Existing reasons cover each mechanism: the area chair's own reading (R01), thin supporting reviews (R04), B-only novelty concerns (R05), shared evidence weighted differently (R06), unanimity read as a higher tier (R12), the dropped weaknesses (R14), the unpenalised [ZCH+20] concession (R16), answerable versus unanswerable concerns (R20) and the single outlying score (R21). The stage 1 candidates map onto these, so no reason is added.
